newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees 3.0 to 3.5 pct economic growth for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees 3.0 to 3.5 pct economic growth for 1996.

text.p: Peruvian Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi said the economy would grow between 3.0 and 3.5 percent this year, compared to 7.0 percent in 1995.
He gave the figure in a speech to Congress.
The government had agreed a target with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) of 3.0 to 4.5 percent growth in 1996.
The Peruvian economy grew 2.0 percent between January and July, compared to 8.7 percent in the same period of 1995, according to the most recent statistics.
Pandolfi added that the government was aiming to achieve six percent growth in 1997 and to bring inflation below 10 percent next year.
Inflation reached 10.23 percent last year, while the cumulative figure for the first eight months of 1996 was 8.84 percent.
